column1: # GE-T5's adjudication sheet — THREE SCRIPTED CODERS, NOT A GOLD.
# §5.5's restated GE-T5 asks whether an engine's agreement with a pooled gold, scored on the
# coders' own scale, is distinguishable from the coders' agreement with each other. That needs
# coders: three of them at least, judging the same pairs independently. S0 had three model
# coders and measured their binary alpha at 0.600, CI [0.550, 0.646] (SMYSL-2.2 §3.7, T1), and
# their sheet is not in this repository.
# The verdicts below were not judged. They are the pool's constructed truth with a disagreement
# written in at fixed intervals — every 6th pair for c1, every 9th for c2, every 13th for c3,
# and three absences — and those intervals were chosen so that alpha over the three columns
# comes out at **0.600**, which is what S0's three model coders actually reached. A scripted
# sheet that agreed perfectly would make the instrument look like it was measuring something.
# So: alpha over these columns is a fact about this file. It is not a fact about any gold, and
# `crates/smysl-text/tests/ge_t5.rs` reports the clause as OWED rather than met when this file
# is the sheet in use. A real sheet drops in with no code change:
#   SMYSL_GE_T5_SHEET=<file.tsv>   three or more coders over the same pairs
# Columns: pair, coder, verdict. A pair is named as `paraphrase.tsv` rows are: `<id>` is that
# planted unit against the King James verse at its own locator, and `<id>+1` against the verse
# next to it — the pool the harness builds by rule, negatives included, so that alpha is not
# computed over a pool that is four-fifths positive. `verdict` is `same` or `not`. A pair a
# coder did not judge is an absent row, not an empty field: alpha treats it as missing, and
# three absences are here so that the path is exercised.
